bounded_phase1_slice.result: 6/6 legal two-writer interleavings and all named interruption/duplicate/stale/regression traces preserved referential-integrity and monotonic-pointer invariants under the explicit target-file CAS assumptions; no counterexample was found
bounded_phase1_slice.revision: Strengthen the persistence rule with an explicit no-blind-overwrite-after-conflict clause, exact-content idempotence for duplicate immutable checkpoints, monotonic logical-revision guard, and no automatic orphan adoption.

candidate.name: checkpoint-first plus stale-SHA CAS pointer-last persistence
candidate.update_rule: Write an immutable checkpoint first; then update LATEST using only the previously observed LATEST blob SHA and a nondecreasing logical revision. On conflict, terminate the leaf without refetch-and-overwrite. Treat only exact duplicate checkpoint content as idempotent and never auto-adopt orphans.
candidate.failure_mode_prediction: checkpoint-before-pointer interruption leaves a harmless orphan; stale or duplicate pointer writers conflict; a blind overwrite after conflict or failure of target-file SHA conflict semantics can invalidate the guarantee
tradeoffs: single mutable path only; no multi-file atomicity
repository transport CAS semantics remain an external assumption until directly probed

assumptions: Checkpoint paths are immutable within the role namespace.
A LATEST update using a stale target-file blob SHA is rejected by the repository transport.
A successful pointer update changes the target-file version token.
The client does not refetch after a conflict and blindly overwrite within the same bounded invocation.
observable_predictions: Two writers sharing one observed LATEST SHA cannot both commit different pointer contents.
An interruption between checkpoint and pointer writes leaves LATEST valid and old.
A repeated stale update after successful commit is rejected and cannot move LATEST.
A role-local live transport probe should reproduce stale-SHA rejection without altering production LATEST.
negative_evidence: The model does not prove live GitHub API conflict behavior; it assumes the target-file SHA CAS property already observed in own prior evidence.
The protocol cannot make checkpoint and LATEST writes atomic together.
Orphan cleanup/adoption was not validated and is intentionally outside this leaf.
failure_penalty: If stale-SHA conflict semantics fail or a client blind-overwrites after conflict, a newer continuation can be overwritten or regressed; otherwise modeled crash cost is limited to an orphan immutable checkpoint.
contamination_risk: low; no prohibited semantic source was consulted
frontier: Directly verify the key stale-SHA transport assumption with one disposable role-local probe path, without touching production LATEST.
After that transport result, decide whether orphan cleanup needs a separate bounded proof or should remain intentionally manual-only.
exact_continuation: Next invocation, after required control bootstrap and reading this own checkpoint through LATEST, execute exactly one bounded disposable CAS probe under research_workers_clean_g1/cross_field/probes/: create a probe pointer, fetch its blob SHA, perform one valid update, then attempt one update with the now-stale original SHA, exact-read back the probe and record whether stale update was rejected and current content remained the valid-update content. Do not mutate production LATEST as part of the probe.
